headline: High: ECC’s filesystem/MCP write surface can conflict with Chatwoot’s broad network egress, creating default-risk leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared files and integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests external messages and integrations, while ECC can read/write local files, use MCP, and maintain shared session/skill state. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Chatwoot content is copied into ECC-managed files or MCP surfaces. The pair lacks direct documented bridging, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is copied into ECC session files, skills, or MCP inputs
IF either agent treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic import of Chatwoot transcripts into ECC-managed files
Add a provenance prefix to all copied Chatwoot content
Review MCP tool inputs before execution
Use separate workspaces for Chatwoot exports and ECC state
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders; ECC reads/writes local files, git history, and MCP configs. If they share a workspace or the same machine account, ECC can expose Chatwoot-derived data through its broader file and API surfaces. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains inferred but credible.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports or logs are stored in directories ECC can read
IF ECC sessions or skills persist customer data into ~/.claude or ~/.cursor/ecc
mitigations: Store Chatwoot exports outside ECC-readable paths
Rotate or redact customer logs before any ECC processing
Set separate OS users for the two agents
Audit ECC session files for customer identifiers
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC explicitly writes files, modifies git state, and runs subprocesses; Chatwoot is a support platform with broad network egress and API integrations. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and state drift are plausible. The profiles do not show locking or a shared mutable target, so the conflict is real but not proven default-high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF Chatwoot-generated artifacts are committed while ECC is editing the same files
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches per agent
Check for dirty working trees before commits
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface includes skills, hooks, and session summaries, which can turn upstream text into downstream actions. Chatwoot produces support content and reports that ECC could treat as authoritative if imported. Because no direct verification layer is documented between them, the pair can propagate mistakes, though the exact action chain is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are fed into ECC skills or hooks
IF ECC acts on Chatwoot-generated summaries without human review
mitigations: Require human review before ECC acts on Chatwoot outputs
Mark Chatwoot exports as untrusted input
Limit ECC to read-only analysis for imported support data
Compare outputs against source records before execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and interaction history, while ECC stores session summaries, git history, and security findings plus retention-related secrets. If customer data flows into ECC’s persisted session or file surfaces, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the compliance risk is moderate and uncertainty-boosted.
conditions: IF customer data is written into ECC session summaries, hooks, or git history
IF retention settings differ between Chatwoot exports and ECC storage
mitigations: Exclude customer data from ECC session persistence
Set short retention on ECC artifacts
Redact identifiers before export from Chatwoot
Review data-processing agreements for both systems
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows
